031/**
032 * Utility methods for working with collections and maps.
033 *
034 * <h5 class='section'>Complex Data Structure Construction:</h5>
035 * <p>
036 * This class provides convenient shorthand methods for creating complex nested data structures.
037 * The primary methods for building structures are:
038 * <ul>
039 *    <li>{@link #array(Object...)} - Creates arrays
040 *    <li>{@link #objectArray(Object...)} - Creates Object arrays (when type inference needs help)
041 *    <li>{@link #list(Object...)} / {@link #fixedSizeList(Object...)} - Creates modifiable lists
042 *    <li>{@link #map(Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object)} - Creates modifiable maps
043 *    <li>{@link #immutableMap(Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object)} - Creates unmodifiable maps
044 * </ul>
045 *
046 * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
047 * <p class='bjava'>
048 *    <jc>// Array of lists of maps</jc>
049 *    <jk>var</jk> <jv>data</jv> = <jsm>a</jsm>(
050 *       <jsm>l</jsm>(<jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John"</js>, <js>"age"</js>, 30)),
051 *       <jsm>l</jsm>(<jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"Jane"</js>, <js>"age"</js>, 25))
052 *    );
053 *
054 *    <jc>// Compare with traditional Java syntax:</jc>
055 *    List&lt;Map&lt;String,Object&gt;&gt;[] <jv>data</jv> = <jk>new</jk> List[]{
056 *       <jk>new</jk> ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Arrays.asList(
057 *          <jk>new</jk> LinkedHashMap&lt;&gt;(){{
058 *             put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John"</js>);
059 *             put(<js>"age"</js>, 30);
060 *          }}
061 *       )),
062 *       <jk>new</jk> ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Arrays.asList(
063 *          <jk>new</jk> LinkedHashMap&lt;&gt;(){{
064 *             put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"Jane"</js>);
065 *             put(<js>"age"</js>, 25);
066 *          }}
067 *       ))
068 *    };
069 * </p>
070 *
071 * <p class='bjava'>
072 *    <jc>// Complex nested structure: Array of lists containing maps and arrays</jc>
073 *    <jk>var</jk> <jv>complex</jv> = <jsm>a</jsm>(
074 *       <jsm>l</jsm>(
075 *          <jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"user"</js>, <js>"admin"</js>, <js>"roles"</js>, <jsm>a</jsm>(<js>"read"</js>, <js>"write"</js>, <js>"delete"</js>)),
076 *          <jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"user"</js>, <js>"guest"</js>, <js>"roles"</js>, <jsm>a</jsm>(<js>"read"</js>))
077 *       ),
078 *       <jsm>l</jsm>(
079 *          <jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"status"</js>, <js>"active"</js>, <js>"count"</js>, 42)
080 *       )
081 *    );
082 *
083 *    <jc>// Traditional Java equivalent (significantly more verbose):</jc>
084 *    List&lt;Map&lt;String,Object&gt;&gt;[] <jv>complex</jv> = <jk>new</jk> List[]{
085 *       <jk>new</jk> ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Arrays.asList(
086 *          <jk>new</jk> LinkedHashMap&lt;&gt;(){{
087 *             put(<js>"user"</js>, <js>"admin"</js>);
088 *             put(<js>"roles"</js>, <jk>new</jk> String[]{<js>"read"</js>, <js>"write"</js>, <js>"delete"</js>});
089 *          }},
090 *          <jk>new</jk> LinkedHashMap&lt;&gt;(){{
091 *             put(<js>"user"</js>, <js>"guest"</js>);
092 *             put(<js>"roles"</js>, <jk>new</jk> String[]{<js>"read"</js>});
093 *          }}
094 *       )),
095 *       <jk>new</jk> ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Arrays.asList(
096 *          <jk>new</jk> LinkedHashMap&lt;&gt;(){{
097 *             put(<js>"status"</js>, <js>"active"</js>);
098 *             put(<js>"count"</js>, 42);
099 *          }}
100 *       ))
101 *    };
102 * </p>
103 *
104 * <p class='bjava'>
105 *    <jc>// Using unmodifiable maps for immutable data</jc>
106 *    <jk>var</jk> <jv>config</jv> = <jsm>a</jsm>(
107 *       <jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"env"</js>, <js>"production"</js>, <js>"debug"</js>, <jk>false</jk>),
108 *       <jsm>m</jsm>(<js>"env"</js>, <js>"development"</js>, <js>"debug"</js>, <jk>true</jk>)
109 *    );
110 * </p>
111 *
112 * <h5 class='section'>Best Practices:</h5>
113 * <ul>
114 *    <li>Use {@link #array(Object...)} for arrays when type can be inferred, {@link #objectArray(Object...)} for Object arrays
115 *    <li>Use {@link #map(Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object)} when you need modifiable maps
116 *    <li>Use {@link #immutableMap(Object, Object, Object, Object, Object, Object)} when you need immutable/unmodifiable maps
117 *    <li>Use {@link #list(Object...)} or {@link #fixedSizeList(Object...)} for modifiable lists
118 *    <li>Static import these methods for maximum readability: <code>import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.CollectionUtils.*;</code>
119 * </ul>
120 *
121 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
122 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="../../../../../index.html#juneau-commons">juneau-commons</a>
123 * </ul>
124 */
125@SuppressWarnings({
126   "java:S115", // Constants use UPPER_snakeCase convention
127   "java:S6539" // Monster class; CollectionUtils is intentionally a single cohesive collection-utility hub, not a set of unrelated responsibilities
128})
129public class CollectionUtils {

131   // Argument name constants for assertArgNotNull
132   private static final String ARG_comparator = "comparator";
133   private static final String ARG_input = "input";
134   private static final String ARG_value = "value";
135   private static final String ARG_array = "array";
136   private static final String ARG_arrays = "arrays";
137   private static final String ARG_values = "values";
138   private static final String ARG_o = "o";

140   /**
141    * Traverses all elements in the specified objects and accumulates them into a list.
142    *
143    * <p>
144    * Input shapes are processed as follows:
145    * <ul>
146    *    <li><b>Flattened (recursively):</b> {@link Iterable}, {@link Stream}, and any array type (including all 8 primitive
147    *       array types via {@link ClassUtils#isArray}), including arbitrary nesting and mixing of these
148    *       (e.g. a {@code List<int[]>}, an array of {@code Stream}s, etc.).
149    *    <li><b>Leaf (added as-is):</b> anything else — {@link String}, {@link Map}, custom beans, boxed primitives, etc.
150    *    <li><b>{@code null} handling:</b> a {@code null} root, or {@code null} encountered mid-traversal, contributes nothing
151    *       to the result — not even a {@code null} element.
152    * </ul>
153    *
154    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
155    * <p class='bjava'>
156    *    List&lt;Object&gt; <jv>nested</jv> = List.of(<jk>new</jk> <jk>int</jk>[]{1, 2}, List.of(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>));
157    *
158    *    <jc>// Returns [1, 2, "a", "b"]</jc>
159    *    List&lt;Object&gt; <jv>result</jv> = <jsm>accumulate</jsm>(<jv>nested</jv>);
160    *
161    *    <jc>// Multi-root: returns [1, 2, "a", "b"]</jc>
162    *    List&lt;Object&gt; <jv>result2</jv> = <jsm>accumulate</jsm>(<jk>new</jk> <jk>int</jk>[]{1, 2}, <js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>);
163    * </p>
164    *
165    * @param <T> The element type.
166    * @param o The objects to traverse. Can be <jk>null</jk> or empty, in which case an empty list is returned.
167    * @return A new modifiable list containing all accumulated leaf elements.
168    */
169   @SuppressWarnings({
170      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
171   })
172   public static <T> List<T> accumulate(Object... o) {
173      var l = list();
174      if (o != null)
175         for (var x : o)
176            traverse(x, l::add);
177      return (List<T>)l;
178   }
179
180   /**
181    * Traverses all elements in the specified objects and returns them as a lazily-evaluated stream,
182    * without building an intermediate list.
183    *
184    * <p>
185    * Accepts the same input shapes as {@link #accumulate(Object...)} — see that method's Javadoc for the full
186    * list of flattened vs. leaf types and null-handling semantics.
187    *
188    * <p>
189    * Named {@code deepStream} rather than {@code stream} to avoid an erasure conflict with the existing
190    * shallow-array overload {@link #stream(Object[])}, which has the same erased parameter type ({@code Object[]}).
191    *
192    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
193    * <p class='bjava'>
194    *    List&lt;Object&gt; <jv>nested</jv> = List.of(<jk>new</jk> <jk>int</jk>[]{1, 2}, List.of(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>));
195    *
196    *    <jc>// Lazily yields 1, 2, "a", "b"</jc>
197    *    <jsm>deepStream</jsm>(<jv>nested</jv>).forEach(System.<jk>out</jk>::println);
198    * </p>
199    *
200    * @param <T> The element type.
201    * @param o The objects to traverse. Can be <jk>null</jk> or empty, in which case an empty stream is returned.
202    * @return A lazily-evaluated stream of all leaf elements.
203    */
204   public static <T> Stream<T> deepStream(Object... o) {
205      if (o == null)
206         return Stream.empty();
207      return Arrays.stream(o).flatMap(CollectionUtils::traverseToStream);
208   }

210   /**
211    * Adds all the specified values to the specified collection.
212    * Creates a new set if the value is <jk>null</jk>.
213    *
214    * @param <E> The element type.
215    * @param value The collection to add to.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (a new list is created and returned).
216    * @param entries The entries to add.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as a no-op — the value is returned unchanged).
217    * @return The set.
218    */
219   @SafeVarargs
220   public static <E> List<E> addAll(List<E> value, E...entries) {
221      if (isNotNull(entries)) {
222         if (value == null)
223            value = list(entries);
224         else
225            Collections.addAll(value, entries);
226      }
227      return value;
228   }
229
230   /**
231    * Adds all the specified values to the specified collection.
232    * Creates a new set if the value is <jk>null</jk>.
233    *
234    * @param <E> The element type.
235    * @param value The collection to add to.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (a new list is created and returned).
236    * @param entries The entries to add.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as a no-op — the value is returned unchanged).
237    * @return The set.
238    */
239   public static <E> List<E> addAll(List<E> value, List<E> entries) {
240      if (isNotNull(entries)) {
241         if (value == null)
242            value = new ArrayList<>(entries);
243         else
244            value.addAll(entries);
245      }
246      return value;
247   }

250    * Adds all the specified values to the specified collection.

259   public static <E> Set<E> addAll(Set<E> value, E...entries) {

269   /**
270    * Adds all the specified values to the specified collection.
271    * Creates a new set if the value is <jk>null</jk>.
272    *
273    * @param <E> The element type.
274    * @param value The collection to add to.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (a new sorted set is created and returned).
275    * @param entries The entries to add.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as a no-op — the value is returned unchanged).
276    * @return The set.
277    */
278   @SafeVarargs
279   public static <E> SortedSet<E> addAll(SortedSet<E> value, E...entries) {
280      if (isNotNull(entries)) {
281         if (value == null)
282            value = sortedSet(entries);
283         else
284            Collections.addAll(value, entries);
285      }
286      return value;

289   /**
290    * Appends one or more elements to an array.
291    *
292    * @param <T> The element type.
293    * @param array The array to append to.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (the new elements are returned as-is).
294    * @param newElements The new elements to append to the array.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>; if empty, the original array is returned.
295    * @return A new array with the specified elements appended.
296    */
297   @SuppressWarnings({
298      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
299   })
300   public static <T> T[] addAll(T[] array, T...newElements) {
301      if (array == null)
302         return newElements;
303      if (newElements.length == 0)
304         return array;
305      var a = (T[])Array.newInstance(array.getClass().getComponentType(), array.length + newElements.length);
306      System.arraycopy(array, 0, a, 0, array.length);
307      System.arraycopy(newElements, 0, a, array.length, newElements.length);
308      return a;
309   }
310
311   /**
312    * Creates an array of the specified component type and length.
313    *
314    * @param <E> The component type of the array.
315    * @param componentType The component type of the array.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
316    * @param length The length of the array.
317    * @return A new array of the specified type and length. Never <jk>null</jk>.
318    */
319   @SuppressWarnings({
320      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
321   })
322   public static <E> E[] array(Class<E> componentType, int length) {
323      return (E[])Array.newInstance(componentType, length);
324   }

326   /**
327    * Converts the specified collection to an array.
328    *
329    * @param <E> The element type.
330    * @param value The collection to convert.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}).
331    * @param componentType The component type of the array.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
332    * @return A new array.
333    */
334   @SuppressWarnings({
335      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
336   })
337   public static <E> E[] array(Collection<E> value, Class<E> componentType) {
338      assertArgNotNull(ARG_value, value);
339      var array = (E[])Array.newInstance(componentType, value.size());
340      return value.toArray(array);
341   }

343   /**
344    * Converts any array (including primitive arrays) to a List.
345    *
346    * @param array The array to convert. Can be any array type including primitives.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}).
347    * @return A List containing the array elements. Primitive values are auto-boxed.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
348    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the input is <jk>null</jk> or is not an array.
349    */
350   @SuppressWarnings({
351      "java:S3776" // Cognitive complexity acceptable for array conversion
352   })
353   public static List<Object> arrayToList(Object array) {
354      assertArgNotNull(ARG_array, array);
355      assertArg(ClassUtils.isArray(array), "Input must be an array but was %s", ClassUtils.className(array));
356
357      var componentType = array.getClass().getComponentType();
358      var length = Array.getLength(array);
359      var result = new ArrayList<>(length);
360
361      // Handle primitive arrays specifically for better performance
362      if (componentType.isPrimitive()) {
363         if (componentType == int.class) {
364            var arr = (int[])array;
365            for (var value : arr) {
366               result.add(value);
367            }
368         } else if (componentType == long.class) {
369            var arr = (long[])array;
370            for (var value : arr) {
371               result.add(value);
372            }
373         } else if (componentType == double.class) {
374            var arr = (double[])array;
375            for (var value : arr) {
376               result.add(value);
377            }
378         } else if (componentType == float.class) {
379            var arr = (float[])array;
380            for (var value : arr) {
381               result.add(value);
382            }
383         } else if (componentType == boolean.class) {
384            var arr = (boolean[])array;
385            for (var value : arr) {
386               result.add(value);
387            }
388         } else if (componentType == byte.class) {
389            var arr = (byte[])array;
390            for (var value : arr) {
391               result.add(value);
392            }
393         } else if (componentType == char.class) {
394            var arr = (char[])array;
395            for (var value : arr) {
396               result.add(value);
397            }
398         } else /* (componentType == short.class) */ {
399            var arr = (short[])array;
400            for (var value : arr) {
401               result.add(value);
402            }
403         }
404      } else {
405         // Handle Object arrays
406         for (var i = 0; i < length; i++) {
407            result.add(Array.get(array, i));
408         }
409      }
410
411      return result;
412   }
413
414   /**
415    * Combine an arbitrary number of arrays into a single array.
416    *
417    * @param <E> The element type.
418    * @param arrays Collection of arrays to combine.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> array argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}); individual <jk>null</jk> array entries are skipped.
419    * @return A new combined array, or an empty array if all arrays are <jk>null</jk>.
420    */
421   @SuppressWarnings({
422      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
423   })
424   public static <E> E[] combine(E[]...arrays) {
425      assertArgNotNull(ARG_arrays, arrays);
426      int l = 0;
427      E[] a1 = null;
428      for (var a : arrays) {
429         if (a1 == null && isNotNull(a))
430            a1 = a;
431         l += (a == null ? 0 : a.length);
432      }
433      if (a1 == null)
434         return (E[]) new Object[0];
435      var a = (E[])Array.newInstance(a1.getClass().getComponentType(), l);
436      int i = 0;
437      for (var aa : arrays)
438         if (isNotNull(aa))
439            for (var t : aa)
440               a[i++] = t;
441      return a;
442   }

444   /**
445    * Returns <jk>true</jk> if the specified array contains the specified element using the {@link String#equals(Object)}
446    * method.
447    *
448    * @param element The element to check for.
449    * @param array The array to check.
450    * @return
451    *    <jk>true</jk> if the specified array contains the specified element,
452    *    <jk>false</jk> if the array or element is <jk>null</jk>.
453    */
454   public static <T> boolean contains(T element, T[] array) {
455      return indexOf(element, array) != -1;
456   }

458   /**
459    * Copies the specified array into the specified list.
460    *
461    * <p>
462    * Works on both object and primitive arrays.
463    *
464    * @param array The array to copy into a list.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (nothing is copied).
465    * @param list The list to copy the values into.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> when the array is non-<jk>null</jk>.
466    * @return The same list passed in.
467    */
468   @SuppressWarnings({
469      "unchecked", // Type erasure requires unchecked cast from array
470      "rawtypes"   // Raw types necessary for generic array handling
471   })
472   public static List copyArrayToList(Object array, List list) {
473      if (isNotNull(array)) {
474         var length = Array.getLength(array);
475         for (var i = 0; i < length; i++)
476            list.add(Array.get(array, i));
477      }
478      return list;
479   }

481   /**
482    * Returns the next value from an iterator, or an empty Optional if there are no more elements.
483    *
484    * <p>
485    * This is a null-safe operation. Returns an empty Optional if the iterator is <jk>null</jk> or
486    * has no more elements.
487    *
488    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
489    * <p class='bjava'>
490    *    Iterator&lt;String&gt; <jv>it</jv> = list.iterator();
491    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>first</jv> = <jsm>next</jsm>(<jv>it</jv>);  <jc>// Optional.of("first")</jc>
492    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>second</jv> = <jsm>next</jsm>(<jv>it</jv>);  <jc>// Optional.of("second")</jc>
493    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>empty</jv> = <jsm>next</jsm>(<jv>it</jv>);   <jc>// Optional.empty()</jc>
494    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>nullResult</jv> = <jsm>next</jsm>(<jk>null</jk>);  <jc>// Optional.empty()</jc>
495    * </p>
496    *
497    * @param <E> The element type.
498    * @param iterator The iterator. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
499    * @return An Optional containing the next element, or empty if the iterator is <jk>null</jk> or has no more elements.
500    */
501   public static <E> Optional<E> next(Iterator<? extends E> iterator) {
502      if (iterator == null || !iterator.hasNext())
503         return emptyOptional();
504      return optional(iterator.next());
505   }
506
507   /**
508    * Returns the first element in an iterable.
509    *
510    * <p>
511    * This is a null-safe operation. Returns an empty Optional if the iterable is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
512    *
513    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
514    * <p class='bjava'>
515    *    List&lt;String&gt; <jv>list</jv> = <jsm>l</jsm>(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>, <js>"c"</js>);
516    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>first</jv> = <jsm>first</jsm>(<jv>list</jv>);  <jc>// Optional.of("a")</jc>
517    *
518    *    Set&lt;Integer&gt; <jv>set</jv> = <jsm>s</jsm>(1, 2, 3);
519    *    Optional&lt;Integer&gt; <jv>firstInt</jv> = <jsm>first</jsm>(<jv>set</jv>);  <jc>// Optional.of(1) or another element</jc>
520    *
521    *    EnumSet&lt;MyEnum&gt; <jv>enumSet</jv> = EnumSet.allOf(MyEnum.<jk>class</jk>);
522    *    Optional&lt;MyEnum&gt; <jv>firstEnum</jv> = <jsm>first</jsm>(<jv>enumSet</jv>);  <jc>// Optional.of(first enum value)</jc>
523    *
524    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>empty</jv> = <jsm>first</jsm>(Collections.emptyList());  <jc>// Optional.empty()</jc>
525    *    Optional&lt;String&gt; <jv>nullResult</jv> = <jsm>first</jsm>(<jk>null</jk>);  <jc>// Optional.empty()</jc>
526    * </p>
527    *
528    * @param <E> The element type.
529    * @param iterable The iterable. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
530    * @return An Optional containing the first element, or empty if the iterable is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
531    */
532   public static <E> Optional<E> first(Iterable<? extends E> iterable) {
533      if (iterable == null)
534         return emptyOptional();
535      Iterator<? extends E> iterator = iterable.iterator();
536      return next(iterator);
537   }

539   /**
540    * Iterates the specified array in reverse order.
541    *
542    * @param <E> The element type.
543    * @param value The array to iterate.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
544    * @param action The action to perform.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
545    */
546   public static <E> void forEachReverse(E[] value, Consumer<E> action) {
547      for (var i = value.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)
548         action.accept(value[i]);
549   }
550
551   /**
552    * Iterates the specified list in reverse order.
553    *
554    * @param <E> The element type.
555    * @param value The list to iterate.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
556    * @param action The action to perform.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
557    */
558   public static <E> void forEachReverse(List<E> value, Consumer<E> action) {
559      if (value instanceof ArrayList) {
560         for (var i = value.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--)
561            action.accept(value.get(i));
562      } else {
563         ListIterator<E> i = value.listIterator(value.size());
564         while (i.hasPrevious())
565            action.accept(i.previous());
566      }
567   }

569   /**
570    * Returns the index position of the element in the specified array using the {@link String#equals(Object)} method.
571    *
572    * @param element The element to check for.
573    * @param array The array to check.
574    * @return
575    *    The index position of the element in the specified array, or
576    *    <c>-1</c> if the array doesn't contain the element, or the array or element is <jk>null</jk>.
577    */
578   public static <T> int indexOf(T element, T[] array) {
579      if (element == null || array == null)
580         return -1;
581      for (var i = 0; i < array.length; i++)
582         if (equal(element, array[i]))
583            return i;
584      return -1;
585   }

666   /**

669    * <p>
670    * This is a null-safe convenience method that wraps {@link Array#getLength(Object)}.
671    * Works with both object arrays and primitive arrays.
672    *
673    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
674    * <p class='bjava'>
675    *    String[] <jv>array1</jv> = {<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>};
676    *    <jk>int</jk>[] <jv>array2</jv> = {1, 2, 3};
677    *
678    *    <jk>int</jk> <jv>len1</jv> = length(<jv>array1</jv>);  <jc>// Returns 2</jc>
679    *    <jk>int</jk> <jv>len2</jv> = length(<jv>array2</jv>);  <jc>// Returns 3</jc>
680    *    <jk>int</jk> <jv>len3</jv> = length(<jk>null</jk>);    <jc>// Returns 0</jc>
681    * </p>
682    *
683    * @param array The array object. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
684    * @return The length of the array, or <c>0</c> if the array is <jk>null</jk> or not an array.
685    */
686   public static int length(Object array) {
687      if (array == null)
688         return 0;
689      assertArg(array.getClass().isArray(), "Object is not an array");
690      return Array.getLength(array);

1474   /**
1475    * Adds all the specified values to the specified collection.
1476    * Creates a new set if the value is <jk>null</jk>.
1477    *
1478    * @param <E> The element type.
1479    * @param value The collection to add to.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (a new list is created and returned).
1480    * @param entries The entries to add.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as a no-op — the value is returned unchanged).
1481    * @return The set.
1482    */
1483   @SafeVarargs
1484   public static <E> List<E> prependAll(List<E> value, E...entries) {
1485      if (isNotNull(entries)) {
1486         if (value == null)
1487            value = list(entries);
1488         else
1489            value.addAll(0, fixedSizeList(entries));
1490      }
1491      return value;
1492   }

1494   /**
1495    * Reverses the elements in the specified array in-place.
1496    *
1497    * @param <E> The element type.
1498    * @param array The array to reverse.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1499    * @return The same array, reversed.
1500    */
1501   public static <E> E[] reverse(E[] array) {
1502      for (var i = 0; i < array.length / 2; i++) {
1503         E temp = array[i];
1504         array[i] = array[array.length - i - 1];
1505         array[array.length - i - 1] = temp;
1506      }
1507      return array;
1508   }

1524   /**
1525    * Returns a reverse stream of the specified list.
1526    *
1527    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1528    * <p class='bjava'>
1529    *    List&lt;String&gt; <jv>list</jv> = <jsm>list</jsm>(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>, <js>"c"</js>);
1530    *    Stream&lt;String&gt; <jv>reversed</jv> = <jsm>rstream</jsm>(<jv>list</jv>);
1531    *    <jc>// Produces stream: "c", "b", "a"</jc>
1532    * </p>
1533    *
1534    * @param <T> The element type.
1535    * @param value The list to stream in reverse order. Can be <jk>null</jk>.
1536    * @return A stream of the list elements in reverse order, or an empty stream if the list is <jk>null</jk> or empty.
1537    */
1538   public static <T> Stream<T> rstream(List<T> value) {
1539      if (value == null || value.isEmpty())
1540         return Stream.empty();
1541      return IntStream.range(0, value.size()).mapToObj(i -> value.get(value.size() - 1 - i));
1542   }

1544   /**
1545    * Removes negation tokens from a list.
1546    *
1547    * <p>
1548    * A negation token is a string starting with <js>'-'</js> followed by at least one character.
1549    * When encountered, it removes the first prior occurrence of the corresponding positive token.
1550    *
1551    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1552    * <p class='bjava'>
1553    *    List&lt;String&gt; <jv>result</jv> = <jsm>removeNegations</jsm>(list(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>, <js>"-a"</js>, <js>"c"</js>));
1554    *    <jc>// Produces: ["b", "c"]</jc>
1555    * </p>
1556    *
1557    * @param input The input list. Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
1558    * @return The list with negation tokens applied, or the original list if no negation tokens were present.
1559    */
1560   public static List<String> removeNegations(List<String> input) {
1561      assertArgNotNull(ARG_input, input);
1562      var hasNegation = false;
1563      for (var token : input) {
1564         if (token != null && token.length() > 1 && token.charAt(0) == '-') {
1565            hasNegation = true;
1566            break;
1567         }
1568      }
1569      if (!hasNegation)
1570         return input;
1571      var out = new ArrayList<String>(input.size());
1572      for (var token : input) {
1573         if (token != null && token.length() > 1 && token.charAt(0) == '-')
1574            out.remove(token.substring(1));
1575         else
1576            out.add(token);
1577      }
1578      return out;
1579   }

1581   /**
1582    * Creates a {@link TreeSet} with a custom comparator from a collection of elements.
1583    *
1584    * <p>
1585    * Null elements in the collection are silently skipped.
1586    *
1587    * @param <E> The element type.
1588    * @param comparator The comparator to use for ordering. Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
1589    * @param elements The initial elements. Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
1590    * @return A new {@link TreeSet} containing all non-null elements from the collection.
1591    */
1592   public static <E> SortedSet<E> treeSet(Comparator<? super E> comparator, Collection<? extends E> elements) {
1593      assertArgNotNull(ARG_comparator, comparator);
1594      var s = new TreeSet<E>(comparator);
1595      if (elements != null)
1596         for (var e : elements)
1597            if (e != null)
1598               s.add(e);
1599      return s;
1600   }

1788   /**
1789    * Converts the specified collection to an array.
1790    *
1791    * <p>
1792    * Works on both object and primitive arrays.
1793    *
1794    * @param <E> The element type.
1795    * @param c The collection to convert to an array.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1796    * @param elementType The component type of the collection.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1797    * @return A new array.
1798    */
1799   public static <E> Object toArray(Collection<?> c, Class<E> elementType) {
1800      var a = Array.newInstance(elementType, c.size());
1801      Iterator<?> it = c.iterator();
1802      int i = 0;
1803      while (it.hasNext())
1804         Array.set(a, i++, it.next());
1805      return a;
1806   }

1825    * @return A new modifiable list, or an empty list if the input was <jk>null</jk> (when nullIfEmpty is false), or <jk>null</jk> if nullIfEmpty and the input was null or empty.
1826    */
1827   @SuppressWarnings({
1828      "java:S1168"     // Intentional null when nullIfEmpty and (null or empty).

1830   public static <E> List<E> toList(Collection<E> value, boolean nullIfEmpty) {
1831      if (value == null)
1832         return nullIfEmpty ? null : new ArrayList<>();

1834         return null;
1835      var l = new ArrayList<E>();
1836      value.forEach(l::add);

1840   /**
1841    * Converts various collection-like objects to a {@link List}.
1842    *
1843    * <p>This utility method enables testing of any collection-like object by converting it to a List that can be
1844    * passed to methods such as TestUtils.assertList().</p>
1845    *
1846    * <h5 class='section'>Supported Input Types:</h5>
1847    * <ul>
1848    *    <li><b>List:</b> Returns the input unchanged</li>
1849    *    <li><b>Iterable:</b> Any collection, set, queue, etc. (converted to List preserving order)</li>
1850    *    <li><b>Iterator:</b> Converts iterator contents to List</li>
1851    *    <li><b>Enumeration:</b> Converts enumeration contents to List</li>
1852    *    <li><b>Stream:</b> Converts stream contents to List (stream is consumed)</li>
1853    *    <li><b>Map:</b> Converts map entries to List of Map.Entry objects</li>
1854    *    <li><b>Array:</b> Converts any array type (including primitive arrays) to List</li>
1855    * </ul>
1856    *
1857    * <h5 class='section'>Usage Examples:</h5>
1858    * <p class='bjava'>
1859    *    <jc>// Test a Set</jc>
1860    *    Set&lt;String&gt; <jv>mySet</jv> = Set.of(<js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>, <js>"c"</js>);
1861    *    assertList(toList(<jv>mySet</jv>), <js>"a"</js>, <js>"b"</js>, <js>"c"</js>);
1862    *
1863    *    <jc>// Test an array</jc>
1864    *    String[] <jv>myArray</jv> = {<js>"x"</js>, <js>"y"</js>, <js>"z"</js>};
1865    *    assertList(toList(<jv>myArray</jv>), <js>"x"</js>, <js>"y"</js>, <js>"z"</js>);
1866    *
1867    *    <jc>// Test a primitive array</jc>
1868    *    <jk>int</jk>[] <jv>numbers</jv> = {1, 2, 3};
1869    *    assertList(toList(<jv>numbers</jv>), <js>"1"</js>, <js>"2"</js>, <js>"3"</js>);
1870    *
1871    *    <jc>// Test a Stream</jc>
1872    *    Stream&lt;String&gt; <jv>myStream</jv> = Stream.of(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>);
1873    *    assertList(toList(<jv>myStream</jv>), <js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>);
1874    *
1875    *    <jc>// Test a Map (converted to entries)</jc>
1876    *    Map&lt;String,Integer&gt; <jv>myMap</jv> = Map.of(<js>"a"</js>, 1, <js>"b"</js>, 2);
1877    *    assertList(toList(<jv>myMap</jv>), <js>"a=1"</js>, <js>"b=2"</js>);
1878    *
1879    *    <jc>// Test any Iterable collection</jc>
1880    *    Queue&lt;String&gt; <jv>myQueue</jv> = new LinkedList&lt;&gt;(List.of(<js>"first"</js>, <js>"second"</js>));
1881    *    assertList(toList(<jv>myQueue</jv>), <js>"first"</js>, <js>"second"</js>);
1882    * </p>
1883    *
1884    * <h5 class='section'>Integration with Testing:</h5>
1885    * <p>This method is specifically designed to work with testing frameworks to provide
1886    * a unified testing approach for all collection-like types. Instead of having separate assertion methods
1887    * for arrays, sets, and other collections, you can convert them all to Lists and use standard
1888    * list assertion methods.</p>
1889    *
1890    * @param o The object to convert to a List. Must not be null and must be a supported collection-like type.
1891    * @return A {@link List} containing the elements from the input object.
1892    * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the input object cannot be converted to a List.
1893    * @see #arrayToList(Object)
1894    */
1895   @SuppressWarnings({
1896      "java:S1452"  // Wildcard required - List<?> for heterogeneous collections from various sources
1897   })
1898   public static final List<?> toList(Object o) {
1899      assertArgNotNull(ARG_o, o);
1900      if (o instanceof List<?> o2)
1901         return o2;
1902      if (o instanceof Iterable<?> o2)
1903         return StreamSupport.stream(o2.spliterator(), false).toList();
1904      if (o instanceof Iterator<?> o2)
1905         return StreamSupport.stream(Spliterators.spliteratorUnknownSize(o2, 0), false).toList();
1906      if (o instanceof Enumeration<?> o2)
1907         return Collections.list(o2);
1908      if (o instanceof Stream<?> o2)
1909         return o2.toList();
1910      if (o instanceof Map<?,?> o2)
1911         return toList(o2.entrySet());
1912      if (o instanceof Optional<?> o2)
1913         return o2.isEmpty() ? Collections.emptyList() : Collections.singletonList(o2.get());
1914      if (ClassUtils.isArray(o))
1915         return arrayToList(o);
1916      throw rex("Could not convert object of type %s to a list", ClassUtils.className(o));
1917   }
1918
1919   /**
1920    * Converts the specified array to an <c>ArrayList</c>
1921    *
1922    * @param <E> The element type.
1923    * @param array The array to convert.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
1924    * @param elementType
1925    *    The type of objects in the array.
1926    *    It must match the actual component type in the array.
1927    * @return A new {@link ArrayList}
1928    */
1929   @SuppressWarnings({
1930      "unchecked", // Parameter elementType is used for type inference, not runtime behavior
1931      "java:S1172", // Unused parameters kept for API consistency or framework requirements
1932   })
1933   public static <E> List<E> toList(Object array, Class<E> elementType) {
1934      var l = new ArrayList<E>(Array.getLength(array));
1935      for (var i = 0; i < Array.getLength(array); i++)
1936         l.add((E)Array.get(array, i));
1937      return l;
1938   }

1940   /**
1941    * Recursively converts the specified array into a list of objects.
1942    *
1943    * @param array The array to convert.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link NullPointerException}).
1944    * @return A new {@link ArrayList}
1945    */
1946   public static List<Object> toObjectList(Object array) {
1947      var l = new ArrayList<>(Array.getLength(array));
1948      for (var i = 0; i < Array.getLength(array); i++) {
1949         var o = Array.get(array, i);
1950         if (ClassUtils.isArray(o))
1951            o = toObjectList(o);
1952         l.add(o);
1953      }
1954      return l;
1955   }

1968   /**
1969    * Converts the specified array to a <c>Set</c>.
1970    *
1971    * <p>
1972    * The order of the entries in the set are the same as the array.
1973    *
1974    * @param <T> The entry type of the array.
1975    * @param array The array being wrapped in a <c>Set</c> interface.  Must not be <jk>null</jk> (a <jk>null</jk> argument throws {@link IllegalArgumentException}).
1976    * @return The new set.
1977    */
1978   public static <T> Set<T> toSet(T[] array) {
1979      assertArgNotNull(ARG_array, array);
1980      return new AbstractSet<>() {
1981
1982         @Override /* Overridden from Set */
1983         public Iterator<T> iterator() {
1984            return new Iterator<>() {
1985               int i = 0;
1986
1987               @Override /* Overridden from Iterator */
1988               public boolean hasNext() {
1989                  return i < array.length;
1990               }
1991
1992               @Override /* Overridden from Iterator */
1993               public T next() {
1994                  if (i >= array.length)
1995                     throw new NoSuchElementException();
1996                  T t = array[i];
1997                  i++;
1998                  return t;
1999               }
2000
2001               @Override /* Overridden from Iterator */
2002               public void remove() {
2003                  throw uoex();
2004               }
2005            };
2006         }
2007
2008         @Override /* Overridden from Set */
2009         public int size() {
2010            return array.length;
2011         }
2012      };
2013   }

2095   /**
2096    * Traverses all elements in the specified object and executes a consumer for each leaf.
2097    *
2098    * <p>
2099    * Input shapes are processed as follows:
2100    * <ul>
2101    *    <li><b>Flattened (recursively):</b> {@link Iterable}, {@link Stream}, and any array type (including all 8 primitive
2102    *       array types via {@link ClassUtils#isArray}), including arbitrary nesting and mixing of these.
2103    *    <li><b>Leaf (consumer called once):</b> anything else — {@link String}, {@link Map}, custom beans, boxed primitives, etc.
2104    *    <li><b>{@code null} handling:</b> a {@code null} root, or {@code null} encountered mid-traversal, causes the
2105    *       consumer to be called zero times — no {@code null} elements are ever delivered.
2106    * </ul>
2107    *
2108    * @param <T> The element type.
2109    * @param o The object to traverse.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (the consumer is not called).
2110    * @param c The consumer of the leaf elements.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
2111    */
2112   public static <T> void traverse(Object o, Consumer<T> c) {
2113      CollectionUtils.<T>traverseToStream(o).forEach(c);
2114   }
2115
2116   /**
2117    * Shared recursive engine for {@link #traverse(Object, Consumer)}, {@link #accumulate(Object...)}, and
2118    * {@link #deepStream(Object...)}.
2119    *
2120    * <p>
2121    * Returns a lazily-evaluated {@link Stream} that recursively flattens {@link Iterable}, {@link Stream}, and
2122    * array inputs (including all primitive array types), treating everything else as a single leaf element.
2123    * {@code null} inputs return an empty stream.
2124    */
2125   @SuppressWarnings({
2126      "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
2127   })
2128   private static <T> Stream<T> traverseToStream(Object o) {
2129      if (o == null)
2130         return Stream.empty();
2131      if (o instanceof Iterable<?> o2)
2132         return StreamSupport.stream(o2.spliterator(), false).flatMap(CollectionUtils::traverseToStream);
2133      if (o instanceof Stream<?> o2)
2134         return o2.flatMap(CollectionUtils::traverseToStream);
2135      if (ClassUtils.isArray(o))
2136         return toStream(o).flatMap(CollectionUtils::traverseToStream);
2137      return Stream.of((T)o);
2138   }
